findings.title: Circulating report answered by staged sight
findings.claim: The scene turns circulating talk into a controlled public encounter: the women are seated and equipped, Joseph is brought into view, and their visual shock becomes bodily evidence.
findings.mechanism: The focus forms link the heard public reputation to preparation, emergence, direct seeing, magnified appraisal, cutting, and hands. The 21:60 and 107:6 connections supply a wider report-to-display frame, while 12:50 and 12:51 return the bodily result to later inquiry.
findings.reader_payoff: The banquet becomes legible as an arranged test whose visible result answers a social report, while the cuts remain an involuntary reaction rather than a decorative detail.
findings.containment: The ordinary hospitality and physical wound remain intact. The evidence supports a staged response and later public use of the result; it does not establish that vindication was her only motive or that the spectacle proves every later claim.

epistemic.reason: The supplied cross-run record is citable and trusted, and all eight branches have exact focus carriers, but the integrated causal relation remains an interpretive synthesis and connection targets lack target morphology.
